question: An operations manager wants Claude to help with the files in one shared folder and is about to connect the company's Google Drive. Which two actions best limit unnecessary exposure? Select two.
options: A) Switch on incognito mode for any conversation that reads files from the connected company Drive.
B) Check what the connecting account can already open in Drive, because Claude inherits that same reach.
C) Obtain whatever approval the organisation's AI policy requires before linking a company data source.
D) Copy the folder's files into the project's knowledge and then delete the originals from the shared Drive.
E) Tell Claude in the prompt to look only at that one folder and rely on it to leave everything else alone.
correct_answers: B) Check what the connecting account can already open in Drive, because Claude inherits that same reach.
C) Obtain whatever approval the organisation's AI policy requires before linking a company data source.
explanations: Incognito affects whether chats are kept and used for improvement; it does not limit what a connected Drive exposes.
Correct. A connector is scoped by the permissions of the account that links it, so the exposure question is what that account can already reach.
Correct on separate grounds: connecting a corporate data source is a governance decision, and most policies require approval before it happens.
Deleting the originals destroys the team's copy of the files and does nothing to narrow what the connector can see.
An instruction in the prompt is not an access control; it does not change what the connector is technically able to reach.
